newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 23.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The tension regarding the customs union between Slovakia and the Czech Republic was alleviated when both sides agreed that Slovakia would not impose quotas on eight agricultural and food products.

- The volume of bad loans in the Czech banking system reached 222 billion crowns at the end of 1996, an increase of three billion crowns since the middle of the year. This is approximately 25 percent of all loans.

- The management of Czech Railways (CD) and union leaders failed to come to an agreement on wage increases during their third meeting on Friday, according to a spokeswoman for CD. This makes the possibility of a strike very real.
- The final week before Christmas once again broke all retail sales records with the greatest interest in small electrical appliances and more expensive brand-name goods.
- Shareholders of Zetor Brno agreed to implement a stabalisation program which will result in a decrease of the company's basic capital from 4.12 billion crowns to 453 million crowns.

- The largest domestic producer of beer, Plzensky Prazdroj a.s., is interested in becoming a strategic partner of Jihoceske Pivovary, th fifth-largest Czech brewery group. Prazdroj intends to increase its shares from the current 22 percent to 40 percent by the year 2000.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Ministry of Finance intends to withdraw the licenses of approximately 20 small investment funds which, even two years following the end of the coupon privitisation program, have not been able to issue their own shares.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Prazske Pivovary exported 270,000 hl of beer by the end of November, an increase of 63 percent over the year before. Three fifths of this export went to Germany, Russia and Slovakia. The greatest increase in exports was to Italy where sales of the company's products increased by 800 percent.
